summary: A narrator describes a group of online users who quickly compile dossiers on people identified by facial recognition after a bank robber's photos are uploaded, while the typhoon also draws attention elsewhere. The narrator explains the Group, an invitation-only, Tor-based community with no written rules or administrators, whose members are smart, funny and strict about avoiding criminal and political attacks. The excerpt ends with the Group investigating the Joint Terrorist Task Force in Minneapolis, where ferret produces preliminary pattern findings after three hours of work.
one_line: A fictional excerpt from Book 14 showing an online Group of hackers crowdsourcing dossiers on a bank robber and then investigating the Joint Terrorist Task Force in Minneapolis.
key_facts: The narrator uploaded three pictures of a bank-robbing, weapon-toting fraudster, which started a race to find information about the people the facial recognition had identified.
The Group's actual name changes every day and is a randomly-generated word, so members usually call it the Group for short.
The Group uses a Tor onion router and encrypts the conversations between members.
The narrator first learned of the Group while on Sourcerer, helping troubleshoot a chat program, when Mattitude sent his public key.
Membership is not totally exclusive and the Group is not a huge secret, but somebody has to let you in.
DoDec reminded members regularly that law enforcement might be monitoring the Group.
Even joking about using the Group for criminal purposes could get a member kicked out, fast and forever.
Faistaff was called out instantly for his crack about launching a distributed denial of service attack on the Department of Justice.
The Group has no administrators and no written rules, only a few basic protocols.
Some older members say the Group is like the internet used to be before it got commercial.
The narrator says the Group is home and family and that this was the first time they asked it for help that was not about code or hardware.
Someone began collecting information on the Joint Terrorist Task Force in Minneapolis, and the file started to fill fast.
ferret, who is really good with data sets and visualization, started a new thread to brainstorm how to find patterns in the collected material.
Three hours later, ferret posted results, described as preliminary but the best guess.
